summary: Week 3 POC sync focused on edge routing perf after kernel bump, telemetry gaps in egress shaping, and security gate checklist. Agreed to run a KV warmup experiment, share traces, and hold a focused security review next week.
transcript:
HEADER: 2027-03-29 15:00 UTC | Duration ~62m | Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Markus Voss (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Dana Lopez (Sable Platform), Rohit Mehra (Sable NetOps), Priya Shah (Sable Security), Ellen Park (Sable PM)

SUMMARY: quick recap, kernel upgrade impact, egress shaping, KV cache warmup, security gates (SOC2, KMS), next steps/action items.

TOPICS: kernel upgrade telemetry, edge routing fallback, KV cache / prefix caching, egress shaping and QoS, audit logs & KMS, pilot acceptance criteria.

00:00 Alice Chen: Alright everyone thanks for joining. I'm gonna run through agenda quick - kernel upgrade results, network shaping, security checklist, then agree next steps.
00:18 Dana Lopez: Yep thanks. We had two customer outages last week, we want to make sure the kernel bump didn't add regressions.
00:27 Markus Voss: Quick note, our kernel bump (v2.17) introduced better attention kernel tiling on the GPUs but we saw some unusual CPU-side scheduling that impacted connection churn in one AZ.
00:40 Rohit Mehra: Yeah that maps to what we saw, a spike in SYN retries and some TCP resets, looked like a late egress queue backlog.
00:53 Jamal Ortiz: To be clear, the runtime picks different kernels based on sequence length distribution so in short bursts the path changed and we saw more small-packet overhead.
01:12 Ellen Park: Sorry, small clarification - is this the same as the "KV cache" warm start we've been discussing?
01:21 Markus Voss: Related but not the same, the KV-cache warmup is about large-context inference and prefix reuse; the kernel change affected per-token latency for short requests which then cascaded into more simultaneous connections.
01:36 Priya Shah: From security, our concern is log fidelity and whether the new path obfuscates any audit logs or changes caller identities. We need to ensure KMS operations are unchanged.
01:51 Alice Chen: Good call. We'll include a KMS check in the rollout notes.
02:03 Dana Lopez: Also, can we get a clearer egress shaping story? We saw abrupt throttling from the edge which triggered fallback to hosted in one zone.
02:15 Markus Voss: Right - the fallback happened because our smart routing policy tripped a circuit breaker on measured egress (we saw packet drops and latency tail). The policy then routed compatible model variants to the hosted tier as a safety net.
02:32 Rohit Mehra: That fallback is fine but it doubles cross-region cost and for us it violates the data residency flow; the RPD flagged that as a non-starter.
02:46 Alice Chen: Understood — we should tighten the fallback policy for your pilot: prefer local degraded model variant first, then fall back cross-region only after X minutes. We'll make that parameterizable.
03:02 Ellen Park: X minutes = ? we need a suggested threshold.
03:07 Markus Voss: From our tests, 30s to 90s is typical, but given your compliance needs I'd recommend 120s with an immediate circuit-breaker alert to NetOps.
03:18 Rohit Mehra: That helps. We'll want a visible metric and alerts in Grafana.
03:25 Jamal Ortiz: We'll add a per-route alert that is tokenized by customer id so you can hook it to your pager.
03:32 Priya Shah: On audit logs - can Redwood guarantee the same event schema post-upgrade? The schema change is our blocker for SOC two attestation.
03:43 Alice Chen: We don't change the schema in a patch release; we'll provide the specific field list and sample events. If needed we can pin the private control plane to the previous logging agent until Sable is satisfied.
03:58 Dana Lopez: That would be great.
04:05 Markus Voss: Back to perf - Jamal, you ran the warmup test overnight?
04:10 Jamal Ortiz: Yes, we primed the KV cache with a synthetic prefix workload. Results: 75% reduction in 99th token latency for long-streaming requests, but short request tail was unchanged.
04:25 Rohit Mehra: Can you share the trace where the short request tail regressed? We need the sample request IDs to correlate with our edge logs.
04:33 Jamal Ortiz: Sure I'll upload the traces; note some request ids are redacted in the export due to PII filtering, but we can provide correlation ids.
04:44 Dana Lopez: The traces will help with QoS shaping - our egress policers are per-namespace and we saw uneven distribution.
04:53 Markus Voss: One idea: add a micro-batching window for short requests at the edge (10-20ms) to reduce small-packet overhead without increasing user-visible latency.
05:04 Rohit Mehra: Micro-batching worries me because of jitter - our real-time flows need tight p95.
05:12 Alice Chen: We can gate micro-batching behind a per-route toggle and only enable for low-priority routes.
05:20 Priya Shah: Security question — what's Redwood's behavior for key rotation in the Private control plane? We need deterministic KMS rotation windows and audit proof.
05:34 Alice Chen: Private deploys integrate with your KMS. Key rotation is controlled by your KMS policy. Redwood will emit key-usage events; we'll collect and show them in the audit export.
05:47 Priya Shah: How about SSO? The pilot currently uses SAML with Okta; any changes from this upgrade?
05:54 Markus Voss: No changes to the control plane auth. We did update the sidecar image but the SAML adapters are unchanged.
06:05 Ellen Park: Great. On acceptance criteria, we want stable <120ms p95 for our 80-token inference workload for three days straight and no cross-region fallbacks except during a planned maintenance window.
06:22 Alice Chen: Noted. We'll log that as the pilot acceptance metric set.
06:29 Dana Lopez: Also need a runbook for kernel rollback that doesn't require a full redeploy.
06:36 Jamal Ortiz: We built a canary rollback path using node draining and image pinning; steps are in the draft doc I'll send today.
06:46 Rohit Mehra: Excellent. Please include the exact kubectl commands; our infra team tends to need the exact incantation.
06:54 Jamal Ortiz: Will do.
07:01 Markus Voss: Quick comment on telemetry gaps: we noticed sampling didn't include TCP retrans counts in the current exporter, so egress backlog visibility is limited.
07:12 Rohit Mehra: That's the one we flagged - please add tcp_retrans and per-socket queue length metrics.
07:20 Alice Chen: We'll push an exporter update and a one-line config change for your prometheus job.
07:26 Priya Shah: For the security review, propose agenda: dataflows, KMS, audit logs schema, retention, SSO mapping, and SCA for the private image.
07:38 Alice Chen: Good. We'll prepare a deck and include the sample events.
07:43 Ellen Park: Can Redwood run a short surge test to reproduce the SYN retry pattern? We'll mark it in our calendar to be ready for it.
07:52 Markus Voss: Yes we can schedule a controlled surge (30min) from our staging harness. Recommend Tuesday 2027-03-30 22:00 UTC to avoid traffic.
07:59 Dana Lopez: That time works for us. We'll have NetOps on standby.
08:05 Alice Chen: ok scheduled.
08:11 Rohit Mehra: One last note - can you put the fallback policy as a tunable in the console with a per-pilot override? We don't want manual config each time.
08:20 Jamal Ortiz: That is on the roadmap; for the pilot we'll expose a per-customer toggle via our private control plane flag.
08:29 Priya Shah: Thanks.
08:32 Alice Chen: Recap — Redwood sends kernel upgrade notes + rollback doc, runs KV warmup test details, adds tcp_retrans metric to exporter, schedules security review, and runs surge test tomorrow. Any other items?
08:47 Ellen Park: None from Sable. Thanks everyone.
08:52 Alice Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts.
08:58 END OF TRANSCRIPT
